item.content:encoded:
The Russians are launching an attack along the border with Poland. Day 1665 of the war

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-16

Reports of Russian forces withdrawing to the Zherebets River line north of Lyman have been confirmed. This has eliminated the encirclement of Sloviansk from the north and has relatively levelled the front line. Most of the territory of the former breach has returned to Ukrainian control, though the Russians still maintain a broad bridgehead on the western bank of the river. According to some sources, the defenders also managed to carry out a series of successful counterattacks in the north-eastern part of Kharkiv Oblast, thereby averting the threat of their forces being encircled.

The Russians have captured part of the territory between the breaches made so far west of Pokrovsk, east of Dobropillia and west of Kostiantynivka, thereby limiting the potential threat posed by Ukrainian counterattacks. The flanking of Druzhkivka has intensified, whilst the invading forces have not achieved much success in Dobropillia or in Mykolaivka, which borders Sloviansk to the east. On 11 September, Russian guided aerial bombs destroyed the railway bridge connecting the eastern and western parts of Sloviansk (the road bridges had previously been destroyed).

Russian forces have entered the centre of Orikhiv, which is currently the scene of fighting. According to some sources, Mala Tokmachka, which neighbours Orikhiv to the east, has also come under their control. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Russia: the second wave of the fuel crisis

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-16

Signs of a deepening fuel crisis have reappeared in Russia since August, with petrol shortages reported in many regions, alongside rising prices and queues at filling stations. The situation deteriorated after Ukraine intensified its attacks on Russian refineries, following a period of partial market stabilisation in mid-July. At least 22 strikes took place in August, the highest monthly number since the start of the war.

As a result, regional authorities and some filling stations have reintroduced fuel rationing. According to Bloomberg, Russian refinery throughput averaged 3.8 million barrels per day (bbl/d) in August, remaining at a low level since June. Before the crisis, the average throughput exceeded 5 million bbl/d. Rosstat reported a renewed increase in petrol prices, which have risen by more than 21% since the beginning of the year. By contrast, an export ban on diesel introduced in July halted the upward trend in diesel prices. Fuel availability at filling stations varies across regions, while available data suggest that supplies to Moscow are being prioritised.

Measures taken by the authorities to ease the crisis – including record fuel imports, lowering emissions standards and regulatory and distribution changes – have proved insufficient. Petrol availability is expected to improve in the coming months as demand declines after the end of the summer season. “Pulaski Policy Papers” is a series of publications that focus on issues of great importance to Poland’s safety and stability, such as: global economy, Poland’s foreign policy and the political situation in Central and Eastern Europe.

The editor-in-chief of the Pulaski Policy Papers is Mr. Tomasz Smura (tsmura@pulaski.pl).

Published: August 26, 2026

What do Poland and the Republic of Korea (ROK) have in common? Despite the distance between the two and the fact that they are representative of and stand as the most successful nations economically, politically and militarily in their respective regions of the world, despite the two nations being the products of two entirely different cultures, the answer to that question of what they have in common is “a great deal.”

item.content:encoded:
Pulaski Commentaries

发布源: 36. Casimir Pulaski Foundation --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-16

Pulaski Commentaries are short analysis of current international developments. The publications are focused on economic and political issues, foreign policy and international security.

Published: September 15, 2026

Since 2022, Russia has systematically attacked Ukraine's energy infrastructure. The first wave of strikes targeted substations, cutting off power distribution; the second hits generating capacity directly. According to data cited by BGK, Ukraine has lost around 70% of its pre-war generating capacity, while gas production fell by around 40% in 2025. The aim of this energy terrorism remains to paralyse the economy and break the will to resist – not only through the hardships caused by restricted access to electricity, water and heating, but through conditions that directly endanger civilians' lives, especially in winter.

Published: September 4, 2026

On 1 September 2026 Bishkek hosted seventeen heads of state and government at the annual summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, the twenty-sixth in its history, convened on the twenty-fifth anniversary of the organisation's founding. The host, Kyrgyzstan, which had just ended its year-long chairmanship, had a few weeks earlier been elected a non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council for 2027 and 2028, while in the same election Germany lost the seat reserved for the Western group.

item.content:encoded:
Defence and International Security

发布源: 36. Casimir Pulaski Foundation --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-16

The Pulaski Foundation Defence and Security Program provides multidisciplinary analysis of the current and emerging defense and security challenges facing the Transatlantic Alliance – with a special focus on Central and Eastern Europe.

Since 2022 the program allocates much of its resources to analysing the possible outcomes and consequences for European security of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. A special component of the program is devoted to the challenges and opportunities facing Poland’s defense policy, including modernizing of the Polish army and its industry. The main goal is to present actionable recommendations to an array of Polish stakeholders, including public administration, which could form a basis for long-term strategies for Poland in times of raising military and defense demands.

Overall, through its analysis, the program advocates for a stronger presence of NATO on the Alliance’s Eastern Flank, more developed European defence capabilities and argues for the need to provide military assistance and solid security guarantees to Ukraine.
